title: Sep 12 Results + Sep 13 Preview: Eighty Percent Is Still Money
summary: 12-3 on Sep 12 with 80% accuracy. Tigers-Rockies rematch headlines tomorrow's slate.

content.value:
## Another Day, Another Statement

Look, I've been around this game long enough to know that 12-3 days don't grow on trees. Eighty percent accuracy on a fifteen-game slate? That's the kind of night that pays the bills and then some. The model caught fire yesterday, and frankly, I'm not surprised—September baseball has patterns if you know where to look.

## The Hits That Mattered

We nailed the Tigers over the Rockies at 63%—file that one away because we're going back to that well tomorrow. The Jays took care of the Orioles exactly as projected, and the Rays handled Houston business at home. Even the coin-flip calls went our way: Nationals over the Angels and Twins over the Guardians, both at 50%, both cashed.

The two misses? Yankees couldn't get past the Mets despite 59% confidence, and the Marlins somehow found a way against the Dodgers. That's baseball in September—even the heavy favorites stumble when rosters get creative.

## Tomorrow's Top Pick: Running It Back in Detroit

Here's where experience matters. When something works, you don't overthink it—you ride it again. The Tigers handled Colorado yesterday at 63%, and tomorrow we're back on Detroit at an even stronger 66% confidence.

Gabriel Hughes gets the ball for the Rockies, while Jackson Jobe takes the mound for Detroit. I've seen this movie before: Colorado pitching on the road in September is not where you want to put your money. The Tigers are playing meaningful baseball, Jobe's been solid at home, and the fundamentals all point the same direction.

This isn't reinventing the wheel. It's reading the room and backing the team that's proven it can handle this exact opponent 24 hours earlier.

content.sub: 66% confidence • Jackson Jobe vs Gabriel Hughes • Motor City stays hot

content.value:
## The Veteran's Take

Eighty percent nights remind you why we trust the process. Not every day will hit like this, but when the model locks in and the fundamentals align, you cash tickets. Period.

Tomorrow we go right back to Detroit because the edge is still there. Hughes versus Jobe isn't a coin flip—it's a calculated advantage. And in this business, advantages compound.

Stay sharp out there.
